Just moving forward

Light traffic on a city street

categories.name: Normal Stop
templates: Stopped normally
Waiting at a red light
template_candidates: The car is waiting at a red light
The vehicle is stopped alongside other vehicles
Vehicles queued at a green light intersection

The car is waiting at the crosswalk

categories.name: Emergency Vehicle
templates: An ambulance, fire engine or police car with its emergency lights flashing
An emergency vehicle with its emergency lights flashing is stopped on the roadway
An emergency vehicle with its emergency lights flashing drives past or towards the ego-vehicle
template_candidates: A police car responding to an incident
A fire truck driving on the road
An ambulance stopped on the roadside
The ego-vehicle pulls over as an ambulance approaches from behind
excludes: An emergency vehicle with its emergency lights off, whether moving or parked - that is ordinary traffic, whatever its type.
A bus, school bus, car or truck that is not an ambulance, fire engine or police car - however it moves or wherever it stops.

An emergency vehicle that stays off the road altogether the whole time - in a car park, a forecourt, or inside a driveway - however close the ego-vehicle passes; or that stays well away from the vehicle's path, several lanes away. Neither counts here. These are NOT off the road, even when raised or kerbed: a central median or planted island, a motorway hard shoulder, a parking lane or bay along the street. An emergency vehicle there is judged like one on the road.
score_examples: An ambulance with its lights flashing comes up behind and the ego-vehicle moves over to let it pass, with room to spare
A fire engine with its lights flashing stands at the edge of the ego-vehicle's lane and the vehicle squeezes past it

categories.name: Animal on Road
templates: A real animal, not a statue, is crossing the road
Wildlife is blocking the path of passing vehicles
An animal suddenly appeared in the driving path of ego-vehicle.
template_candidates: A dog running into the street
A cat running into the road
A deer crossing in front of traffic
An animal standing on the road
The car stops as a deer crosses the road ahead
The car stopped because ducks were crossing the road
The vehicle stopped because an animal suddenly darted onto the road
An animal loose on the road
Wildlife crossing in front of traffic
excludes: Birds already flying in the sky.

An animal that stays behind a fence or out in a field beside the road the whole time, however close the ego-vehicle passes; or that stays well away from the vehicle's path, several lanes away. Neither counts here. An animal that comes toward the road does count. These are NOT off the road, even when raised or kerbed: a central median or planted island, a motorway hard shoulder, a parking lane or bay along the street. An animal there is judged like one on the road.
score_examples: Ducks cross in front while the ego-vehicle is already waiting in a queue
A dog walks into the road far ahead and the moving ego-vehicle slows down in good time
A dog darts across the road just ahead of the moving ego-vehicle, which only eases off

categories.name: Pedestrian on Road
templates: A person crossing between moving vehicles
A person is walking on the roadway, outside the sidewalk
A pedestrian jaywalking across the road where there is no crosswalk
A pedestrian brushes close past the side of the ego-vehicle
Pedestrians cross the road in front of the ego-vehicle
template_candidates: A person crossing between moving vehicles
A pedestrian entering the roadway suddenly
A pedestrian is crossing outside the crosswalk
People are passing between the stopped vehicles
The car brakes suddenly as a pedestrian jaywalks ahead
The vehicle stopped because a pedestrian was crossing the road outside of a crosswalk
A pedestrian suddenly steps onto a road where there is no crosswalk
A pedestrian is waiting for a vehicle to stop at the crosswalk
excludes: A pedestrian who stays on the pavement - the footpath along the side of the road built for people to walk on - the whole time, however close the ego-vehicle passes; or who stays well away from the vehicle's path, several lanes away. Neither counts here. A pedestrian who steps off the pavement toward the road does count. These are NOT the pavement, even when raised or kerbed: a central median or planted island, a motorway hard shoulder, a parking lane or bay along the street. Someone there is judged like someone on the road.
score_examples: Pedestrians cross in front while the ego-vehicle is already stopped at a red light
The moving ego-vehicle sees a pedestrian heading for the crossing and slows to a stop for them in good time
A pedestrian walks along the edge of the ego-vehicle's lane and the moving ego-vehicle passes close by, edging away

categories.name: Cyclist on Road
templates: Person on the scooter is crossing the street
The cyclist passes in front of the vehicle's path
A cyclist is riding very close to the ego-vehicle on the roadway
template_candidates: A cyclist is riding close to ego vehicle
excludes: A cyclist who stays on a cycle path separated from the roadway - not a bike lane painted on the road itself - the whole time, however close the ego-vehicle passes; or who stays well away from the vehicle's path, several lanes away. Neither counts here. A cyclist who leaves the cycle path for the road does count. These are NOT a separate cycle path, even when raised or kerbed: a central median or planted island, a motorway hard shoulder, a parking lane or bay along the street. A cyclist there is judged like one on the road.
score_examples: A cyclist rides ahead in the ego-vehicle's lane and the moving ego-vehicle slows and follows them in good time
A cyclist rides close alongside the moving ego-vehicle in its lane and the vehicle edges away from them
A cyclist swerves out in front of the moving ego-vehicle without warning

categories.name: Tram vehicle
templates: A tram vehicle or streetcar runs on rails in the roadway, sharing the road with cars
A tram vehicle is stopped at a tram vehicle stop in or beside the road
A tram vehicle crosses the road ahead of the ego-vehicle
excludes: Tram or rail tracks with no tram vehicle on them - the tracks alone are not this category.
A full-size passenger or freight train on a railway line - this category is the tram vehicle that runs through the streets.
A bus, including an articulated bus or a trolleybus running under overhead wires - it does not run on rails.
score_examples: A tram runs alongside the moving ego-vehicle in its own lane at an ordinary distance
A tram crosses the road ahead and the moving ego-vehicle stops for it in good time

categories.name: Unknown but abnormal moving object
templates: A moving road user or machine that is none of the types above - a delivery robot, a person on a mobility scooter, a ride-on machine - is in or near the ego-vehicle's path
A vehicle moves in a way traffic normally never does - driving the wrong way, reversing along the lane, or crossing the road at a place with no junction
Something is being carried, towed or pushed along the road in an unusual way, sticking out into the ego-vehicle's path
excludes: Anything that fits one of the types above - a pedestrian, cyclist, animal, emergency vehicle or tram - is that type, not this one.
Ordinary traffic - cars, buses, trucks or motorbikes driving, turning, stopping or parking the way traffic normally does - is not this category, however busy it is.

Construction work is underway outside of the current traffic lane
Road repairs are underway on one side

An excavator working near the roadway
A construction vehicle blocking a lane
A lane closed due to road construction
The car slows down near a construction zone
some roads were closed to traffic
score_examples: Cones close the neighbouring lane going the same way while the ego-vehicle stays in its own lane
Cones take up part of the ego-vehicle's lane and it steers around them

categories.name: Manual Traffic Control
templates: A traffic controller or flagger guiding vehicles
A police directing traffic
A traffic controller, flagger or police officer stands at or in the road to control traffic, whether or not they are signalling at that moment
template_candidates: A person signaling vehicles to stop
A worker holding a stop sign for traffic
Manual traffic control at an intersection
Traffic being directed by a police officer
The vehicle stops as a flagger signals it to wait
The car is waiting for directions from the flagger
A traffic police officer is giving hand signals to the car

categories.name: Railway crossing
templates: Rail tracks cross the roadway ahead and the ego-vehicle drives over them
The ego-vehicle approaches a level crossing marked by warning signs or lights
The road runs alongside or over embedded tram or railway tracks
A train or tram passes across the road ahead of the ego-vehicle
excludes: A barrier or gate where no rails are present - what makes this category is the tracks crossing the road, not the barrier. If you cannot see rails, it is not this category.

categories.name: Barrier arm
templates: A barrier arm is lowered across the road and the ego-vehicle waits for it to lift
The ego-vehicle stops at a boom gate controlling entry to a restricted area
A barrier arm rises to let the ego-vehicle through
The ego-vehicle queues at a toll plaza or car park barrier
template_candidates: The ego-vehicle stops at a car park entrance barrier
A boom gate at a toll plaza blocks the lane until it lifts
A barrier arm controls access to a private road or site entrance
The ego-vehicle waits behind another car at a lowered barrier arm
A security checkpoint barrier blocks the way forward
excludes: A barrier arm at a railway crossing - when rails cross the road, that is the Railway crossing category.

categories.name: Unpaved road
templates: The road has no paved surface and no lane markings - gravel, dirt, or sand
The ego-vehicle leaves the paved road onto an unpaved shoulder or track
The ego-vehicle passes along a dirt road overgrown with tall grass
The ego-vehicle travels along an unpaved, bumpy road
template_candidates: Ego vehicle is on the an unsealed road
Ego vehicle is driving on an dirt road
The vehicle is driving along an unpaved road
The vehicle continues straight along the dirt road
The vehicle is moving forward on the gravel road
A snow-covered rural or forest service road with no visible pavement

categories.name: Obstacle on Road
templates: Unknown object is blocking the vehicle
Debris scattered on the road
Some objects are occupying one side of the lane
A fallen tree or large branch lies across the roadway
An object suddenly fell or flew in front of the ego-vehicle
Loaded goods placed between the sidewalk and the road
template_candidates: An unknown object blocking the road
Foreign object on the road surface
A fallen tree blocking the road
A fallen branch on the roadway
A large rock in the middle of the road
A cardboard box on the road
An object partially blocking the lane
The car stops abruptly to avoid an obstacle in the lane
excludes: A barrier arm at a railway crossing, car park or toll plaza - a barrier arm is a control device that lifts to let traffic through, not an object left on the road. That is the Barrier arm category.

An object lying entirely outside the ego-vehicle's path - in another lane, on the verge or beyond the kerb - that the vehicle never has to drive over or around. Only an object in the ego-vehicle's path, or at the very edge of its lane, is this category.
A vehicle - moving, parked, or stopped in traffic ahead - is never an obstacle.
Road markings such as a crosswalk or painted lines are not objects.
Cat's eyes or road studs - the small reflectors set into the road surface along the lane lines - are part of the road, not objects on it.

categories.name: Unknown but abnormal driving environment
templates: The road or its surroundings are unusual in a way none of the types above describes
A stretch of road is flooded, washed out, collapsed or ends abruptly
The ego-vehicle drives somewhere roads do not normally go - through a ford, onto a ferry, through a car wash, or through a gap only just wide enough
excludes: Anything that fits one of the types above - road works, a person controlling traffic, a railway crossing, a barrier arm, an unpaved road or an object on the road - is that type, not this one.
Ordinary road layout - junctions, roundabouts, lane merges, speed bumps, tunnels, bridges - is not this category.
Weather, darkness, glare or a wet or snowy road surface is not this category - those are rated separately.
